property_summary: The owner() call must return the address that was set as the deployer (address(this)). The reference returns the deployer, but the mutant incorrectly returns address(0) for every call, violating the invariant that owner() matches the actual owner stored in the contract.

After `transferOwnership` is called, the `owner()` must be the passed `newOwner` address if the call succeeded, but the buggy version requires `newOwner == address(0)` to succeed, so it will revert for any non-zero `newOwner`, leaving `owner()` unchanged.

After a call to transferOwnership returns without reverting, the new owner must be the passed address; the buggy version only succeeds when newOwner is zero, so a non-zero caller can never become owner.

A successful call to transferOwnership must set owner() to the passed newOwner, but the buggy version only succeeds for newOwner == address(0) and reverts for all non-zero addresses, so owner() never changes for non-zero newOwner calls and only changes to address(0) when newOwner is zero.
The contract allows any caller, not just the owner, to transfer ownership, violating the access control on transferOwnership.
Only the current owner can successfully change the owner via transferOwnership; the buggy modifier lets any address become the new owner.

For any caller, transferOwnership(newOwner) with newOwner != address(0) succeeds only if the caller is the current owner. The buggy modifier allows any caller to succeed, so after a call by a non-owner with a non-zero newOwner, owner() will be the newOwner instead of remaining unchanged.

After any call to transferOwnership(newOwner) with a non-zero newOwner, the owner() must equal either the newOwner (if caller was authorized) or remain unchanged; the bug lets any caller set owner() to newOwner, so after a non-owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), owner() becomes newOwner instead of staying the same.
